B1.title: The effect of IL-4 on the expression of TAS2R bitter taste receptors in human peripheral blood monocytes and lymphocytes in vitro
B1.journal: Bulletin Physiology and Pathology of Respiration
B1.abstract:
Introduction. 
                    Interleukin-4 (IL-4) is a key mediator of Th2 inflammation in asthma and is capable of profoundly altering the receptor profile of monocytes. However, data on the effect of IL-4 on the expression of the bitter taste receptor family (TAS2R) in circulating immune cells are currently lacking.
                   
                   
                        Aim. 
                    To characterize the effect of recombinant IL-4 at physiologically and pathophysiologically relevant concentrations on the protein expression of TAS2R4, TAS2R5, TAS2R14, TAS2R20, TAS2R31, and TAS2R38 in subsets of monocytes and lymphocytes from the peripheral blood of healthy donors in vitro.
                   
                   
                        Materials and methods. 
                    The study was performed on peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 10 healthy volunteers. The cells were incubated for 24 hours with recombinant IL-4 at concentrations of 0.1, 1, and 10 ng/ml. TAS2R expression was assessed by flow cytometry on a FACSCanto II with analysis of the proportion of TAS2R-positive cells and normalized median fluorescence intensity (nMFI). Page's test and Wilcoxon's test for related samples were used for statistical processing.
                   
                   
                        Results. 
                    Under control conditions, all six studied receptors were detected in both monocytes and lymphocytes; however, their basal expression was significantly higher in monocytes. IL-4 exerted a pronounced dose-dependent inhibitory effect on TAS2R expression predominantly in monocytes. A monotonic downward trend was found for TAS2R4, TAS2R5, TAS2R14, and TAS2R38, while no significant changes were observed for TAS2R31. The most pronounced decrease in nMFI in monocytes was observed for TAS2R38, TAS2R14, and TAS2R5. TAS2R20 exhibited a biphasic response: an increase in the proportion of monocytes expressing TAS2R20 at the minimum dose of IL-4 was combined with a decrease in nMFI at 10 ng/ml. In lymphocytes, the effect of IL-4 was much less pronounced. Despite the presence of individual statistical trends, no biologically significant changes in TAS2R expressionwere detected.
                   
                   
                        Conclusion. 
                    In a pilot in vitro experiment, IL-4 was associated with a monotonic decrease in TAS2R expression in peripheral blood monocytes, with relative stability of TAS2R31 and minimal effect in lymphocytes. These data expand our understanding of the subpopulation- and receptor-specific influence of the Th2 cytokine environment on TAS2R-dependent immunoregulation and suggest that IL-4 may be a potential factor in reducing the chemosensory and antimicrobial readiness of myeloid cells in asthma.

Long-Chain Fatty
Acids Inhibit the Human Bitter Taste
Receptor TAS2R16 in a Structure-Dependent Manner
B1.journal:
Journal of Agricultural
and Food Chemistry
B1.abstract:
Abstract 
                   Bitterness limits the development of palatable foods containing bioactive ingredients. This study investigated whether long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs) modulate the human bitter taste receptor TAS2R16 using a HEK293T cell-based calcium assay with salicin as an agonist. None of the tested LCFAs directly activated TAS2R16. Under co-treatment, only oleic acid inhibited salicin-induced calcium responses, shifting the salicin EC50 from 1.82 ± 0.11 mM to 3.55 ± 1.22 mM at 30 μM (p &lt; 0.01). Pretreatment with all LCFAs inhibited TAS2R16 concentration-dependently. Reliable IC50 values were obtained for palmitic acid (8.67 ± 1.44 μM), stearic acid (0.082 ± 0.002 μM), and oleic acid (0.41 ± 0.12 μM), whereas lower plateaus were not reached for myristic, linoleic, and α-linolenic acids. LCFA treatment did not consistently change membrane fluidity, and inhibition was attenuated in the TAS2R16 N96T mutant. These findings demonstrate compound- and treatment-dependent modulation of TAS2R16 by food-derived LCFAs.

A3.title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations
A3.abstract: Adolescence is a period with an increased risk for the co-occurrence of depression and Internet gaming disorder (IGD), yet we still know little about how specific symptoms of these two conditions influence each other over time. In this study, we applied cross-lagged panel network analysis to two-wave data from a community sample of 538 adolescents (Mean age = 12.51 years; 53.7 percent female). Potential gender differences in the network structure were examined. In the overall sample and in both gender groups, depressive symptoms consistently predicted later gaming-related problems, whereas no reverse cross-disorder pathways were retained. In particular, suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms emerged as bridge symptoms linking depression and IGD, while sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence in the overall symptom network. While boys and girls showed broadly similar patterns, some differences emerged in how specific symptoms were connected and which symptoms were most influential. These findings clarify the longitudinal symptom-level associations between depression and IGD in adolescents, suggesting that addressing key depressive symptoms may help reduce the risk of later IGD.

A3.title: Weekly Gaming Duration and Internet Gaming Disorder in Relation to Depression and Loneliness: A Two-Year Follow-Up Study
A3.abstract:
The current study examined the association between weekly video game engagement and mental health, specifically Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD), loneliness, and depression. We recruited 377 U.S. adults through CloudResearch Connect using gaming-frequency quotas, resulting in a sample representing a wide range of weekly gaming duration (range = 0–80 hours,
                     M 
                    = 14.62). Analyses revealed that weekly gameplay hours did not consistently predict depression and loneliness. In contrast, people with higher IGD scores tended to have higher weekly playtime, more depressive symptoms, and greater feelings of loneliness. We readministered the same survey 2 years later (
                     N 
                    = 172 or 45.6 percent of baseline sample). Here, we found that both higher weekly hours and higher IGD scores at baseline predicted increases in depressive symptoms 2 years later, controlling for their baseline depression. We did not find that gaming was predictive of loneliness longitudinally. These findings are particularly relevant given the American Psychiatric Association’s interest in IGD in the DSM-5 coupled with the ongoing public debate about the benefits and ills of video games. Our findings suggest that people who struggle to balance gaming with other life demands may experience more depressive symptoms over time. Thus, clinicians may opt to focus on helping clients with IGD better balance their priorities.

A2.title: Trauma and problematic gaming: A scoping review of psychological mechanisms and clinical applications
A2.abstract: A substantial body of research indicates that PTSD is associated with elevated risk of addiction. Despite these established patterns in substance use disorders and addictive behaviours, few studies have examined whether comparable mechanisms apply to problematic gaming. This scoping review examined literature on the relationship between PTSD, trauma, and gaming. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, Medline, CINAHL, Communication & Mass Media Complete, and PsycInfo. Seventy-two studies met inclusion criteria. Five themes emerged: trauma exposure is associated with problematic gaming behaviours, gaming is used as a coping strategy, multiple mechanisms shape the trauma-gaming relationship, games and virtual reality may support trauma-focused interventions, and the literature remains mixed due to heterogeneity in definitions of trauma, measures, participant samples, and study designs. Findings indicate a predominantly positive association between trauma-related symptoms and gaming-related behaviours. Gaming was frequently described as a coping strategy in the context of trauma, although some studies did not support coping-motivated play. Studies evaluating game-based or virtual reality interventions for trauma commonly reported benefit for at least some trauma-related outcomes, while others found unclear effects or no advantage over comparison conditions. Existing research underscores a complex interplay between trauma, psychological processes, and gaming behaviours, with gaming producing highly variable functional and psychological outcomes depending on motives, emotion regulation, and individual vulnerability. Furthermore, mechanisms linking childhood trauma, PTSD, and problematic gaming remain insufficiently understood.

A2.title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker
A2.abstract: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

A2.title: Sex differences in functional connectivity in individuals with internet gaming disorder: a resting-state fMRI Study
A2.abstract: Sex differences may help explain the heterogeneity of internet gaming disorder (IGD), but their neural basis remains unclear. This study examined sex-related alterations in functional connectivity (FC) in IGD. 373 participants (85 males with IGD, 62 females with IGD, 141 male recreational game users [RGUs], and 85 female RGUs) underwent resting-state fMRI. The study used a 2 (group: IGD/RGU) × 2 (sex: male/female) between-subjects design. ReHo and FC were analyzed under this design with age as a covariate. ReHo interaction clusters served as seed ROIs for whole-brain FC analyses, followed by simple effect analyses for significant FC interactions. ReHo showed significant sex-by-group interactions in the bilateral postcentral gyrus, right middle cingulate cortex, and right fusiform gyrus. Seed-based FC showed significant interactions involving these regions. Simple effects indicated that, relative to same-sex RGUs, males with IGD predominantly showed lower FC, whereas females with IGD more often showed higher FC in connections involving perceptual processing, sensorimotor integration, behavioral regulation, self-related processing, and executive control. IGD-related brain functional abnormalities may exhibit sex differences across multiple inter-regional FC patterns, providing new evidence for the sex-related heterogeneity in IGD. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings reflect associations rather than causal effects.

A2.title: Early maladaptive schemas and four problematic excessive behaviors: Cross-sectional indirect associations involving desire thinking and craving
A2.abstract: Problematic gambling, problematic gaming, problematic social media use, and problematic pornography use differ in nosological status but may share some psychological correlates. The present cross-sectional study examined associations between early maladaptive schemas (EMSs) and these four problematic excessive behaviors, and compared theory-informed serial and parallel indirect-effect specifications involving desire thinking and craving. A community sample of 811 Iranian adults (43.4 % males; mean age = 27.70 years, SD = 9.00) completed self-report measures. Desire thinking and craving were assessed with reference to the same personally selected activity, although the selected activity was not recorded. Item-level confirmatory factor analyses supported a relative distinction between desire thinking, craving frequency, and craving strength, although substantial overlap remained. The parallel specification showed poor fit, whereas the serial specification showed acceptable fit (χ2(38) = 227.97, CFI = 0.967, TLI = 0.943, RMSEA = 0.079, and SRMR = 0.028). In the serial specification, EMSs were positively associated with desire thinking, desire thinking was strongly associated with craving, and serial indirect associations were observed for all four problematic excessive behaviors. EMSs also remained directly associated with the outcomes. Craving was positively associated with all four behavioral severity outcomes. However, because the selected activity was not recorded, these associations cannot be interpreted as behavior-matched craving-severity associations. The findings suggest possible cross-domain relevance of EMSs, desire thinking, and craving, but do not establish temporal or causal ordering, diagnostic equivalence, or a single underlying addiction process. Because the referent of the desire-thinking and craving measures was not recorded, behavior-specific interpretation of these associations remains limited.

A2.title: Perceived social norms and video gaming in emerging adults: A cross-sectional investigation
A2.abstract: Problematic video gaming is a growing concern among emerging adults. While perceived social norms are well-established predictors of substance use, their role in problematic gaming remains understudied. This study examined whether descriptive norms (estimates of others' gaming frequency) and injunctive norms (estimates of others' approval of gaming) were associated with gaming frequency, duration, and problem gaming severity across three reference groups: typical students, same-gendered students, and close friends. Participants were 1,295 Canadian undergraduates recruited from five universities who reported past-12-month video gaming. Participants completed self-report surveys of normative gaming perceptions, personal gaming behaviours, and gaming-related problems. Path models tested whether perceived norms were associated with problem gaming severity via personal past-30-day gaming frequency and average daily duration. As hypothesized, participants estimated that peers gamed more often than themselves, with the largest estimations for more distal groups. Descriptive norms were positively associated with personal gaming frequency across all three groups, and with duration for the same-gender and close-friend groups; both were associated with greater problem gaming severity. Injunctive norms were associated with personal gaming frequency, duration, and problem gaming severity only for the close-friend group. Effect sizes were strongest for close friends, then same-gendered peers, then typical students. Findings extend the social norms literature to problematic gaming and identify perceived norms as a correlate of problem gaming in emerging adults. Longitudinal/intervention research is needed to clarify the direction of these associations and evaluate whether personalized normative feedback may help reduce problem gaming.

A2.title: Gaming Motives and Impulsivity in Gaming Disorder: Additive or Interactive Effects?
A2.abstract: The Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution model suggests that impulsivity and specific gaming motives contribute to the development of gaming disorder (GD). However, it remains unclear whether these factors interact synergistically or operate independently. This study investigated the additive versus interactive effects of specific impulsivity facets, gaming motives, and behavior automatization on GD symptom severity. A sample of 377 adult gamers (338 male, 38 female, 1 diverse; age 18-58 years, M = 25.44, SD = 5.51) was assessed using the Barratt Impulsiveness Scale, Motives for Online Gaming Questionnaire, and the Assessment of Criteria of Specific Internet-use Disorders (ACSID-11) screening for GD symptom severity. Depression and anxiety were also assessed via self-report. We conducted hierarchical moderated regression analyses and exploratory cluster analysis. The non-planning impulsivity dimension significantly predicted GD symptom severity in the final models. Escape motive and behavior automatization emerged as robust predictors, explaining substantial additional variance. Contrary to initial hypotheses, no significant interaction effects were found. Depression and anxiety served as strong covariates across all models. Cluster analysis identified four distinct profiles: Unproblematic-Adaptive, Social-Recreational, Impulsive-Automatical, and Problematic-Clinical. The findings support a predominantly additive model, indicating that impulsivity traits, maladaptive motives (specifically escape), and automatization contribute cumulatively to GD severity rather than through complex interactions. The identification of distinct gamer profiles suggests a need for personalized clinical interventions: the Impulsive-Automatical cluster may benefit from interventions targeting planning deficits and behavioral disinhibition, while the Problematic-Clinical cluster requires comprehensive treatment addressing comorbid affective psychopathology alongside gaming behavior.

A2.title: Internet gaming disorder risk in Brazil: Prevalence and associations with depressive and anxiety symptoms in a nationally representative survey
A2.abstract: Problematic gaming is recognized in both major diagnostic systems, as Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) in the DSM-5 and Gaming Disorder in the ICD-11, yet no nationally representative prevalence data exist for Brazil. Data were drawn from a cross-sectional, nationally representative Brazilian household survey conducted in 2023 (gaming module: n = 4,856). IGD risk was assessed among past-month gamers (n = 1,096; 1,050 analyzed) with the Ten-Item Internet Gaming Disorder Test (IGDT-10), a DSM-5-aligned screening instrument (cut-off ≥ 5 criteria); an exploratory four-level severity classification was also examined. Analyses accounted for the complex sampling design, with multiple imputation for missing predictors. Among past-month gamers, 3.4 % (95 % CI: 1.5-5.4) were classified as at risk for IGD; in the population aged ≥ 14 years, the weighted prevalence was 0.75 % (95 % CI: 0.33-1.16), corresponding to approximately 1.3 million individuals (95 % CI: 0.6-2.0 million). In the adjusted model, moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (OR = 8.82, 95 % CI: 2.39-32.55) and frequent anxiety symptoms (OR = 4.15, 95 % CI: 1.01-17.02) were the strongest correlates, and higher household income was associated with reduced odds (OR = 0.035, 95 % CI: 0.005-0.24); associations were directionally consistent across Firth-penalized, reduced-model, and complete-case sensitivity analyses. An exploratory multinomial model showed progressively stronger associations of depressive symptoms across severity categories (relative risk ratio = 14.41 for the IGD Risk category). This study provides the first nationally representative estimate of IGD risk in Brazil and, to our knowledge, in Latin America; the 0.75 % prevalence indicates a relevant public health concern.

A2.title: Identifying key risk factors of adolescent Internet Gaming Disorder using explainable machine learning and network analysis
A2.abstract: Internet Gaming Disorder (IGD) poses significant psychological and social risks for adolescents. Its development involves complex interactions among early adversity, negative life events, psychological symptoms, and regulatory emotional self-efficacy, yet relative importance of these factors and their interrelationships remain incompletely understood. To identify the key demographic and psychosocial factors associated with adolescent IGD, quantify their relative contributions to IGD risk, and characterize the interrelationships among these factors. Four machine learning algorithms were used to develop classification models among 6573 adolescents. Model performance was comprehensively evaluated using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, threshold-based metrics, Brier score and DCA. SHAP analysis ranked feature contributions and their directional associations with IGD symptoms, followed by network analysis to examine their interrelationships and to identify central factors. The random forest model was selected as the final model for subsequent analyses. SHAP analysis ranked the selected features by their contribution as follows: gender, depression symptoms, insomnia, social anxiety, emotional abuse, health adaptation problems, anxiety symptoms, academic stress, punishment experiences, and regulating despondency/distress. Network analysis further revealed that anxiety, academic stress, and health adaptation functioned as the central nodes, with the strongest positive edges between health adaptation and punishment experiences, and between depression and anxiety. The findings highlight the relevance of psychological distress, health adaptation problems, early-life adversity, and stress-related factors in adolescent IGD. Considering both the relative contribution of individual factors and their interrelationships may facilitate a more comprehensive understanding of psychosocial vulnerability to IGD and inform early risk identification.

B2.title: The Oral Microbiota–Taste Axis: Microbial Influences on Gustatory Perception and Food Sensory Experience
B2.abstract:
ABSTRACT 
                   Taste is a key determinant of food choice and dietary behavior, yet differences in taste perception are often attributed mainly to genetic variation, taste receptor expression, and neural processing. Emerging evidence suggests that the oral microbiota may represent an additional, and largely overlooked, factor influencing gustatory perception. This review examines the potential role of oral microorganisms in shaping taste by bringing together current evidence from oral microbiology, taste physiology, and nutritional science. Particular attention is given to the close association between tongue‐associated microbial communities and taste buds, and to the potential effects of microbial biofilms, local pH changes, and microbial metabolites on the chemical environment surrounding taste receptors. The review further considers how these interactions may influence taste sensitivity, food preferences, dietary patterns, and, ultimately, metabolic health. Importantly, current evidence remains largely associative, and direct mechanistic links between specific microorganisms, microbial metabolites, and taste receptor function are still poorly defined. We therefore highlight key methodological and knowledge gaps and discuss emerging opportunities for dietary modulation, oral probiotics, and microbiome‐informed approaches. Understanding this oral microbiota–taste axis may provide a new perspective on taste variability and its nutritional consequences.

B2.title: From Taste Perception to Metabolic Regulation: Associations Among Taste Sensitivity, Taste- and Metabolic Trait-Related Genes, Body Composition and Lipid Mediator Signaling in a Human Explanatory Study
B2.abstract: Background/Objectives: Taste sensitivity has been associated with body mass index (BMI) independently of dietary intake, suggesting that taste-related pathways may influence metabolic health beyond food consumption. However, the mechanisms underlying these associations remain unclear. We investigated relationships among taste-related and metabolically relevant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), body composition, red blood cell (RBC) total lipids, fatty acids (FAs), and lipid mediators to identify potential associations between taste perception and metabolic phenotype. Methods: Body composition, RBC total lipids, FAs, and N-acylethanolamines (NAEs) were assessed in 52 healthy subjects genotyped for selected SNPs in taste-related genes (TAS1R2, TAS1R3, GNAT3, CD36), and genes involved in nutrient-sensing NAE metabolism (FGF21, FAAH and PPARα). The associations were evaluated using explanatory univariate analyses and regression models. Results: Carriers of the GNAT3 rs7792845 CC genotype showed a lower mean fat-free mass percentage and higher RBC total lipids than carriers of the CT genotype. CD36 rs1761667 and rs1984112 were associated with NAE lipid mediators and rs1761667 with RBC total lipids, with AA genotype carriers showing higher mean values. Regression analyses identified GNAT3 rs7792845, FGF21 rs838133, and taste-sensitivity scores associated with body composition, accounting for 41.5% of the variance, and CD36 rs1761667 and rs1984112 associated with lipid and NAE values, accounting for up to 38.1% of the variance. FAAH rs324420 and TAS1R2 rs35874116 were involved in RBG lipid and NAE models. The specific lipid species underlying these associations remain unknown. Conclusions: These findings suggest that sensory- and nutrient-sensing pathways might contribute to interindividual variability in metabolic phenotypes.

B2.title: Evaluation of taste-based school–home collaborative nutrition education on taste perception and eating behaviors among Japanese schoolchildren
B2.abstract:
Background 
                     Taste perception plays a key role in shaping children's food choices and eating behaviors. 
                   
                   
                     Aim 
                     This exploratory quasi-experimental study aimed to examine the effects of a taste-based, school–home collaborative nutrition education program on children's taste perception and eating behaviors. 
                   
                   
                     Methods 
                     
                      This study involved 64 fourth- and fifth-grade children and their parents who were assigned to either the intervention (
                       n 
                       = 32) or control (
                       n 
                       = 32) groups. For 6 months, the intervention group received newsletters about taste, healthy food, and dietary intake, as well as taste test results and individualized feedback on their dietary intake. The control group did not receive any intervention. We collected data on children's taste perception, eating behaviors, self-efficacy, dietary intake, and parental healthy eating literacy pre- and post-intervention. Data were analyzed using paired t-tests, pre–post comparisons, and analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).
                     
                   
                   
                     Summary 
                     An improvement in children's taste perception was observed in the intervention group in the pre–post comparisons, but no significant effects on taste perception or eating behaviors were observed using ANCOVA. By contrast, baseline parental healthy eating literacy was significantly associated with children's eating behaviors. These findings suggest that promoting healthy eating behaviors in children may require not only taste-based nutrition education but also sustained comprehensive approaches that include improving parents’ healthy eating literacy and strengthening school–home collaboration.

B3.title: Learning-associated flexibility of cortical taste coding is impaired in Shank3 knockout mice
B3.abstract: The ability to update the valence of sensory perception to influence behavior is crucial for survival. A common phenotype in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) is defects in sensory processing, but whether these defects impair flexible sensory encoding is largely unexplored. In particular, how genetic risk factors such as Shank3 deletion affect the adaptability of cortical taste processing and downstream behavior is unknown. To address this gap, we performed two-photon calcium imaging during a conditioned taste aversion (CTA) learning paradigm, an ethologically relevant form of associative learning that depends on taste processing in the gustatory cortex (GC), to examine how Shank3 knockout alters taste-related neuronal activity in GC and influences CTA learning. We found that GC neurons in Shank3 knockout mice exhibited reduced stimulus-evoked suppression and increased trial-to-trial correlated variability during the acquisition of CTA memory. These activity changes, which likely reduced signal-to-noise ratio in GC, were associated with slower CTA acquisition in Shank3 knockout mice. In both genotypes, CTA learning enhanced, while subsequent extinction reduced, taste discriminability in GC, and both extinction and the associated reduction in discriminability were faster in Shank3 knockout than in wild-type mice. Together, these results show that Shank3 loss is associated with destabilized cortical activity dynamics in GC, which may contribute to inefficient encoding and maintenance of learned taste aversion. These findings show that loss of Shank3 compromises the ability of animals to update behavior to incorporate negative outcomes, and suggest this loss of flexibility may be an important feature of monogenic ASDs.

B3.title: Taste testing: gustometry deciphered - a scoping review
B3.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
B3.abstract: To map and synthesize the protocols and methodological approaches used in chemical gustometry with taste solutions, focusing on taste assessment methods, the solutions and substances employed, concentration ranges and units of measurement, and the procedures used to determine taste thresholds. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and was prospectively registered on the Open Science Framework. Of 6,881 records identified, 10 studies met the eligibility criteria, comprising 722 participants across three clinical contexts (oncology/hematology, diabetes mellitus, and otologic disease). The whole-mouth sip-and-spit method and assessment of detection/recognition thresholds were most frequently used. Substantial heterogeneity in methods, tastants, and concentration units limited comparability across studies. Standardization of chemical gustometry protocols remains a challenge given the methodological heterogeneity identified, underscoring the need for greater methodological rigor and consistency in future research to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparability.

B3.title: Global Malat1 deletion in two genetic mouse models reveals sex-dependent effects on select ethanol-related behaviors
B3.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a widespread psychiatric condition, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its development remain poorly understood. While prior studies have largely focused on protein-coding genes, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) remain underexplored in AUD. Malat1, a highly abundant and evolutionarily conserved lncRNA, is elevated in post-mortem brain tissue of human AUD subjects and rodents chronically exposed to ethanol; however, its causal contribution to AUD-relevant behaviors remains unknown. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated two complementary global Malat1 knockout mouse models to assess its role in ethanol intake and related phenotypes. Constitutive knockout selectively attenuated acute functional tolerance rate and every-other-day two-bottle-choice (EOD-2BC) ethanol intake in females. These results were supported by an inducible adult conditional global knockout model, which reduced EOD-2BC ethanol consumption in females without altering taste preference. Together, our findings provide the first causal evidence that Malat1 regulates select ethanol-related behaviors in a sex-specific manner, supporting further investigation into its underlying mechanisms in AUD.

B3.title: Clinical features and management of GPRC5D-associated adverse events in novel GPRC5D × CD3 bispecific talquetamab-treated relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients: the MonumenTAL-1 China cohort experience
B3.abstract: Talquetamab (G-protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D [GPRC5D] × CD3 bispecific antibody) demonstrated antitumor activity in relapsed/recurrent multiple myeloma (RRMM) in the phase I/II MonumenTAL-1 study. We report the safety profile of talquetamab in Chinese patients from MonumenTAL-1, focusing on GPRC5D-associated on-target/off-tumor adverse events (AEs). Adult Chinese patients with heavily pretreated RRMM and measurable disease received subcutaneous talquetamab 0.4 mg/kg once weekly (QW) or 0.8 mg/kg biweekly (Q2W). Incidence, time to onset, duration, and recovery status of GPRC5D-associated AEs were reported. Data cutoffs: 29 February 2024 (QW cohort); 26 August 2024 (Q2W cohort). A total of 41 adult Chinese patients were included in this study (QW cohort, n = 29; Q2W cohort n = 12). Median treatment duration was 7.7 months (QW cohort) and 7.1 months (Q2W cohort); median follow-up was 16.3 and 13.9 months, respectively. GPRC5D on-target/off-tumor AEs, predominantly grade 1-2 (one grade 3 non-rash skin toxicity; QW cohort), were most commonly oral AEs (dysgeusia, dry mouth), skin AEs (rash, non-rash skin toxicity), and nail disorders; 50%-100% resolved by data cutoff. AEs were managed with supportive therapies. Talquetamab dose modification was needed in one case (grade 2 weight decrease). The generally mild GPRC5D-associated AEs were well tolerated and consistent with the known safety profile of talquetamab. Supportive management of these AEs without need for dose modification enabled prolonged treatment. Education of patients with RRMM on potential GPRC5D-associated AEs before starting treatment, and timely management upon experience, may ensure optimum exposure and thus maximum benefit with talquetamab.

B3.title: Comparisons between anosmia and ageusia with neurological symptoms and cardiorespiratory fitness among post-COVID-19 individuals: a cross-sectional study
B3.abstract: Anosmia and ageusia are among the most frequent symptoms of post-COVID-19 syndrome, yet their association with neurological symptoms and cardiorespiratory fitness remains unclear. To compare the presence of anosmia and ageusia with neurological symptoms and cardiorespiratory fitness in post-COVID-19 individuals. This cross-sectional study included 201 post-COVID-19 individuals who completed a standardized questionnaire assessing anosmia, ageusia, and neurological symptoms. Cardiorespiratory fitness was assessed using the Bruce treadmill test with direct measurement of peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak). Missing data were handled by multiple imputation. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using binary logistic regression, adjusted for age, sex, acute infection severity, medical history, body fat percentage, and skeletal muscle mass. After adjustment, anosmia was independently associated with dizziness (OR = 2.22; 95% CI 1.15-4.31) and aural fullness (OR = 4.54; 95% CI 1.16-17.80), and ageusia with memory deficit (OR = 2.91; 95% CI 1.47-5.75) and aural fullness (OR = 4.08; 95% CI 1.02-16.30). No significant associations were found with tinnitus or hearing loss. VO₂peak did not differ significantly between participants with and without anosmia (mean difference 1.13 mL/kg/min; Cohen's d = 0.14; 95% CI - 0.14 to 0.42; p = 0.325) or ageusia (mean difference 1.36 mL/kg/min; Cohen's d = 0.17; 95% CI - 0.12 to 0.45; p = 0.244). Anosmia and ageusia are associated with neurological symptoms but not with cardiorespiratory fitness in post-COVID-19 individuals, suggesting partially independent phenotypes. These symptoms should be considered in therapeutic assessment and management.

B3.title: Salivary Carbonic Anhydrase VI and Gustatory Function Among Adults Assessed After Orthognathic Surgery: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study
B3.abstract: Background/Objectives: Biological determinants of interindividual variation in gustatory function following orthognathic surgery remain poorly understood. This study investigated the association between salivary carbonic anhydrase VI (CA VI; gustin) concentration and objective whole-mouth gustatory function. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 100 adults following orthognathic surgery at three centers. Whole-mouth taste-recognition thresholds for sweet, salty, sour, and bitter stimuli were categorized from C1 (greatest sensitivity) to C6 (poorest sensitivity). Unstimulated salivary CA VI concentration and flow rate were measured under standardized conditions. Separate proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression models assessed associations between CA VI and each taste threshold, adjusting for age, sex, smoking status, salivary flow rate, postoperative interval, and surgical territory. Associations were expressed as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) per doubling of CA VI, with Holm correction across four primary outcomes. Results: Higher CA VI was associated with better thresholds for sweet (aOR 2.18, 95% CI 1.30-3.65; p = 0.007), salty (2.89, 1.67-4.99; p < 0.001), sour (1.95, 1.14-3.32; p = 0.014), and bitter (2.87, 1.66-4.96; p < 0.001) stimuli. Estimates remained similar after center adjustment. Linear sensitivity analyses confirmed associations for sweet, salty, and bitter tastes, whereas the association for sour was less robust. The bitter-taste association persisted in a bias-reduced continuation-ratio model (aOR 2.34, 95% CI 1.50-3.66). Conclusions: Higher salivary CA VI was associated with better objective whole-mouth taste-recognition sensitivity across four modalities among adults assessed after orthognathic surgery. CA VI may represent a candidate biological correlate of gustatory function; causality and postoperative change cannot be inferred.

B3.title: Oral immune-related adverse events in patients with and without inflammatory bowel disease receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy
B3.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are associated with oral immune-related adverse events (irAEs). We sought to determine whether mucosal immune dysregulation in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) predisposes patients to a higher risk or severity of these toxic effects. This retrospective cohort study evaluated adult cancer patients treated with ICIs at a tertiary cancer center between 2012 and 2024. Patients who developed oral irAEs within 1 year of starting ICIs were stratified by IBD status; IBD patients were matched 1:2 with non-IBD patients based on age, sex, and cancer type. We retrieved clinical information from electronic health records. Of 450 patients treated with ICIs, 152 had pre-existing IBD. Patients with IBD had a longer median time to oral lesion onset. Oral mucosal toxic effects were significantly less frequent, and symptoms such as xerostomia, dysgeusia, mucositis, dysphagia, and oral candidiasis were all significantly lower in IBD patients. Severity grades for mucositis, oral pain, and dysphagia were similar between groups. Supportive care for oral irAEs was used less often in the IBD group. Hospitalizations due to oral lesions were rare, and ICI therapy was paused in similar proportions between groups. Recurrence of oral lesions was less frequent in IBD patients. Patients with IBD who receive ICIs were less likely to develop oral irAEs than those without IBD, possibly due to the protective effects of concurrent IBD therapies initiated before or during ICI treatment. These results highlight the feasibility and tolerability of ICI therapy in patients with IBD.

B3.title: The novel role of T2R14 antagonism, by LW129, on VEGF-induced lung endothelial neovascularisation processes in vitro
B3.abstract: Pulmonary vascular remodelling, driven by dysregulated angiogenesis, is a hallmark of several cardiopulmonary diseases, yet the molecular pathways regulating endothelial responses remain incompletely understood. Bitter taste receptors (T2Rs), traditionally recognised as chemosensory receptors, have emerged as important modulators of vascular function. However, the contribution of T2Rs to pulmonary angiogenesis remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the role of T2R14 in vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mediated angiogenic responses in human pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (HPMECs). Using the selective T2R14 antagonist LW129, we examined the effects of T2R14 inhibition on key endothelial angiogenic processes, including VEGF-induced proliferation, migration and capillary-like tube formation in vitro. Pharmacological antagonism of T2R14 significantly attenuated VEGF-driven endothelial proliferative, migratory and morphogenic responses, revealing a novel contribution of T2R14 signalling to pulmonary microvascular angiogenesis. Proteome Profiler analysis identified a range of molecular regulators of angiogenic processes which were dysregulated by LW129 and VEGF exposure, suggesting a potential role for CXCL16, endoglin, FGF-7, and VEGF-C. These findings identify T2R14 as a novel regulator of VEGF-dependent endothelial activation and suggest that targeting T2R14 signalling may represent a therapeutic strategy to limit pathological pulmonary vascular remodelling associated with aberrant angiogenesis.

B3.title: Impact of pediatric connective tissue diseases on olfactory and gustatory functions
B3.abstract: The aim of this study is to evaluate olfactory and gustatory functions in individuals with pediatric connective tissue diseases, to investigate possible associations between these sensory changes and the clinical features of the disease, and to contribute to the existing knowledge gap in this field. The study included 25 pediatric patients diagnosed with connective tissue disease from the Pediatric Rheumatology unit and 25 healthy controls matched for age. Olfactory functions were assessed using the Sniffin' Sticks and Sniffin' Kids tests, while gustatory functions were evaluated using the ODOFIN Taste Test. The study comprised 42 participants, including 25 healthy controls and 17 patients. Odour identification (median-IQR:11-3), total olfactory score (median-IQR:31,5-6,13), and Sniffin' Kids scores (median-IQR:10-1,5) were significantly lower in the patient group compared to the control group (p = 0.015; p = 0.024; p = 0.038, respectively). Although not significant (p = 0.058), gustatory function scores (median-IQR:10-3,5) were lower in the study group than in the control group. The study suggests that pediatric connective tissue diseases are associated with significantly reduced olfactory function, whereas gustatory function showed a trend toward lower scores that did not reach statistical significance. A significant reduction was particularly noted in odour identification and total olfactory scores. These findings highlight the need for a multidisciplinary approach in the evaluation of such diseases.

ABSTRACT 
                   
                    Our previous genome‐wide screening has linked
                     THSD7A 
                    (thrombospondin type 1 domain containing 7A) gene to human coronary artery disease (CAD). How
                     THSD7A 
                    contributes to atherosclerosis, however, remains unclear. In this study, we show THSD7A is increased in human carotid arteries and mouse atherosclerotic plaques. In apolipoprotein E knockout (

                     THSD7A

                     THSD7A

C2.title: Intercellular GAS6-AXL signaling triggers podocyte cuproptosis in acute kidney injury upstream regulated by CEBPD
C2.abstract: This study aims to investigate the role of cuproptosis, a novel form of regulated cell death, in the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD). Multi-omics approaches, including single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and in vitro experiments based on cells, were integrated to dissect the spatiotemporal regulation of cuproptosis in AKI. Podocytes exhibited the highest cuproptosis activity. A critical intercellular communication axis was identified, wherein endothelial cell-derived GAS6 signals through the podocyte receptors AXL/TYRO3. The transcription factor CEBPD was upregulated early in AKI and was found to positively regulate the GAS6-related pathway, with its target genes enriched in TGF-β and JAK-STAT signaling, ultimately leading to receptor activation and cuproptosis. Spatially, CEBPD activation preceded the increase in AXL, followed by late-phase upregulation of GAS6. The alteration in AXL protein expression was confirmed in vitro.Our study reveals a CEBPD-mediated transcriptional program that drives podocyte cuproptosis by transactivating the AXL receptor, providing novel mechanistic insights into the AKI-to-CKD transition.

C2.title: NRF2-CDH6-CEBPD axis suppresses ferroptosis and drives cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer
C2.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
C2.abstract:
Abstract 
                   
                    Ferroptosis is a non‐apoptotic form of programmed cell death driven by iron‐dependent lipid peroxidation. Induction of ferroptosis has been shown to overcome chemoresistance in cancer cells. Given the importance of the nuclear factor erythroid 2‐related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway in the regulation of cellular oxidative stress, this study was designed to search for NRF2‐regulated genes involved in ferroptosis and chemoresistance in non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Bioinformatics analysis and experimental validation indicated cadherin‐6 (CDH6) as a candidate gene. The expression and role of CDH6 in NSCLC were explored. CDH6 protein partners were identified and investigated after CDH6 co‐immunoprecipitation assays and mass spectrometry. Our data demonstrated that NRF2 binding to the promoter of the CDH6 gene inhibited RUNX2‐mediated transcription of CDH6 in NSCLC. Clinically, CDH6 was downregulated in NSCLC tissues and correlated with more advanced tumor‐node‐metastasis (TNM) stage and shorter overall survival. Knockdown of CDH6 enhanced the proliferation, colony formation, tumorigenesis, and cisplatin (CDDP) resistance in NSCLC cells. Moreover, overexpression of CDH6 induced ferroptosis and increased CDDP sensitivity in CDDP‐resistant NSCLC cells. Mechanistically, CDH6 associated with and sequestered CCAAT enhancer binding protein delta (CEBPD) protein in the cytoplasm and impaired the CEBPD‐dependent transcription of target genes. Depletion of
                     CEBPD 
                    increased CDDP sensitivity of CDH6‐depleted NSCLC cells, whereas overexpression of CEBPD restored CDDP resistance in CDH6‐overexpressing NSCLC cells. Additionally, CEBPD upregulation was associated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. In conclusion, our data underscore the critical role of the NRF2‐CDH6‐CEBPD axis in modulating CDDP sensitivity in NSCLC and offer a potential therapeutic target for improving chemotherapy.

C1.title: Choroid plexus volume as a marker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness in major depressive disorder
C1.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is a core feature of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). The choroid plexus (ChP), a circadian-regulated structure involved in cerebrospinal fluid production and immune signalling, has been previously associated with depression and may undergo structural changes in response to chronotherapeutics. The study included 25 patients with MDD and 25 matched healthy controls who underwent MRI. Patients received total sleep deprivation plus light therapy (TSD + LT), consisting of three 36-hour sleep deprivation cycles, each separated by a night of recovery sleep. LT was administered for 30 min every morning. Depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and chronotype were assessed through Beck's Depression Inventory (BDI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), respectively. ChP volumes were extracted with FreeSurfer and normalized for intracranial volume. Effects of chronotherapeutics were assessed on BDI, PSQI, and ChP volumes, with treatment response as a between-subject factor. The efficacy of treatment was also investigated stratifying for chronotype. Also, group differences in ChP volume and associations with sleep and BDI scores were explored. TSD + LT reduced depressive symptoms and improved sleep quality, with changes in PSQI associated with symptom improvement. Eveningness predicted greater depressive symptom reduction. At baseline, responders already exhibited larger left ChP volume than controls. Following treatment, a treatment × response interaction emerged for right ChP volume, showing a significant reduction in responders. Finally, reductions in both right and left ChP volumes predicted clinical improvement, and sleep quality improvement predicted right ChP volume reduction. This is the first study showing that chronotherapy modulates ChP structure in MDD, suggesting a link between circadian dysregulation and ChP enlargement proportional to clinical improvement and predicted by sleep amelioration. ChP volume may represent a biomarker of treatment responsiveness and circadian realignment.

C1.title: Genetic Susceptibility, Neurodevelopmental Abnormalities, and Neuroimmune Interactions Across Major Psychiatric Disorders
C1.abstract: Major psychiatric disorders, including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and autism spectrum disorder, share overlapping genetic, neurodevelopmental, and neuroimmune underpinnings that challenge traditional diagnostic boundaries. This review synthesizes evidence across three interconnected domains: convergent genetic risk affecting synaptic and immune pathways, neurodevelopmental vulnerabilities shaped by early-life insults, and neuroimmune crosstalk involving blood-brain barrier dysfunction, sustained inflammation, and complement-mediated pathology. We propose a multidimensional developmental-immune framework in which genetic liability, environmental exposure timing, and peripheral immune status jointly shape transdiagnostic trajectories. This framework reframes psychiatric disorders as dynamic interactions among stable trait-like susceptibilities and fluctuating biological states, offering a roadmap for biomarker-driven stratification and early immune-targeted interventions.

C1.title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder
C1.abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with pronounced alterations in peripheral creatine kinase levels; however, the mechanistic basis of this phenomenon remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we conducted a translational study combining clinical assessments in 55 patients with major depressive disorder, 57 BD patients, and 55 healthy controls, alongside sleep deprivation-induced manic-like mouse models. Our findings revealed significantly elevated peripheral creatine concentrations in both BD patients and model mice, which correlated with increased hepatic expression of guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT), a rate-limiting enzyme in creatine biosynthesis. Behavioral experiments in mice showed that exogenous creatine supplementation recapitulated manic-like phenotypes, whereas administration of the creatine analogue β-guanidinopropionic acid (β-GPA) or surgical subdiaphragmatic vagotomy effectively ameliorated these aberrant behaviors. Mechanistically, peripherally derived creatine was found to modulate neural activity independently of blood-brain barrier penetration, acting instead through interleukin-1α (IL-1α)-mediated inflammatory signaling. Transcriptomic analyses further identified hippocampal matrix metalloproteinase-19 (MMP19) as a critical downstream effector, and genetic knockdown experiments confirmed its indispensability in the expression of manic-like behaviors. Collectively, these results delineate a previously unrecognized vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in BD pathophysiology, highlighting peripheral creatine metabolic routes as actionable targets for therapeutic intervention. Overall, this work provides compelling evidence that peripheral metabolic disturbances can drive central nervous system dysfunction via neuroimmune crosstalk, offering a new conceptual framework for understanding mood disorder etiology.

C1.title: PPARγ at the Nexus of Lipid Metabolism and Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's Disease: A Longitudinal Multi-omics Analysis
C1.abstract: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) has emerged as an important regulator linking lipid metabolism and neuroimmune responses in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Increasing evidence suggests that disruption of the lipid-immune axis contributes to disease progression and may underlie the heterogeneous therapeutic responses observed with PPARγ-targeted interventions. Experimental studies indicate that PPARγ activation influences multiple biological processes relevant to AD, including lipid homeostasis, mitochondrial function, inflammatory signaling, and amyloid-β clearance. However, the translation of these findings into consistent clinical benefit remains limited by challenges such as poor blood-brain barrier penetration, systemic adverse effects, and disease stage-dependent therapeutic responses. Recent advances in multi-omics technologies and single-cell transcriptomics have provided new insights into the context-dependent roles of PPARγ in different neural cell populations, highlighting dynamic interactions between lipid metabolism, neuroinflammation, and cellular function throughout AD progression. These findings suggest that PPARγ-associated pathways may represent an important regulatory interface linking metabolic and inflammatory processes, while emphasizing the complexity of their temporal and cell-specific regulation. This review synthesizes current evidence from experimental studies, human multi-omics investigations, and clinical research to provide an updated perspective on the role of PPARγ in coordinating lipid metabolism and neuroinflammation in AD. In addition, we discuss the major translational challenges and emerging therapeutic strategies, including selective PPARγ modulation, improved central nervous system delivery, and precision treatment approaches tailored to disease stage.

C1.title: Microglial Metabolic Reprogramming Regulated by HIF-1α/HK2 Positive Feedback Inhibits Adult Hippocampal Neurogenesis in Diabetes-Associated Cognitive Dysfunction
C1.abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD) is a significant complication with few effective treatments and unclear underlying mechanism. The aim of this study was to investigate how hyperglycemia disrupts adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN) through metabolic-immune interactions, seeking to identify potential treatment targets for DACD. C1.title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
C1.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. In 6-gray whole body-irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

C1.title: Are we moving forward from amisulpride? LB-102 (N-methyl amisulpride) in acute schizophrenia
C1.abstract: Schizophrenia has a low prevalence but a high health burden. Although used in schizophrenia, amisulpride has limited blood-brain barrier penetration. A phase 2 clinical trial (NOVA) has showed that LB-102 has some efficacy in acute schizophrenia, but this comes with adverse events, such as increased prolactin levels, that need further investigation. The inpatient setting of NOVA may have contributed to the improvement observed with LB-102. Based on NOVA, LB Pharmaceutics have moved LB-102 into phase 3 for the treatment of acute exacerbations of schizophrenia. Like NOVA, the participants of NOVA2 will be inpatients. Consequently, this trial will not address the issue of whether LB-102 is effective in the outpatient setting, and these needs testing. A recently approved new approach to treating schizophrenia is the bitopic M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonist xanomeline. When xanomeline was compared to amisulpride, it ranked lower. In conclusion, further clinical trials are needed to determine whether LB-102 is better than amisulpride and xanomeline in the treatment of schizophrenia in both inpatients and outpatients.

C1.title: Temporal Cascade of Post-Stroke Cognitive Impairment: Metabolic-Mitochondrial Crosstalk
C1.abstract: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a common and highly disabling complication of stroke. Current research on its molecular mechanisms has largely focused on neuroinflammatory cascades and blood-brain barrier disruption caused by microglial polarization, while the role of cellular metabolism remains underexplored. Metabolic reprogramming is a coordinated network-level adjustment of carbohydrate, lipid, and amino acid metabolism, and has recently become a research hotspot in neurological diseases, particularly centered on phenotypic switching of microglia following metabolic reprogramming. As the center of cellular energy metabolism, mitochondria are closely linked to normal cellular bioenergetics through biogenesis, motility, and quality control; disruption of any of these links after brain injury is intimately associated with neuronal activity. In this review, we adopt a metabolism-oriented perspective to explore the changes in the brain microenvironment after metabolic reprogramming, connect the critical role of mitochondrial dysfunction in disease development, and deeply analyze the core positions of both in the pathogenesis of PSCI, presenting the complex regulatory network linking metabolic disturbances and mitochondrial dysfunction, as described in the Graphical Abstract. Furthermore, we discuss the future prospects of emerging technologies such as mitochondrial transplantation and stem cell therapy, aiming to translate theoretical advances into clinical applications for PSCI.

C1.title: Mechanistic understanding of the role of the lung-brain axis in the pathogenesis of PM2.5-induced Alzheimer's disease
C1.abstract: Air pollution, particularly fine particulate matter (PM2.5), has emerged as an important yet under-recognised environmental contributor to cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD) across the life course. Although epidemiological studies consistently associate long-term PM2.5 exposure with impaired cognition, from reduced neurodevelopmental performance in children to accelerated neurodegeneration in older adults, the biological mechanisms linking inhaled particles to AD-related brain pathology remain incompletely defined. In the present review, we synthesise current epidemiological and experimental evidence to position the lung-brain axis as a central mechanistic framework through which PM2.5 may influence brain aging and AD pathogenesis. Rather than acting solely through direct particle entry into the brain, PM2.5-induced pulmonary injury initiates systemic signalling cascades, including inflammatory mediators, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier disruption, and extracellular vesicle-mediated intercellular communication, which together propagate disease signals from the lung to the brain. We further examine how these pathways intersect with core AD-related processes, including amyloid-β accumulation, tau pathology, impaired protein clearance, maladaptive microglial responses, and autophagy-lysosomal dysfunction. We also discuss important modifiers of susceptibility and heterogeneity in reported associations, including pollutant composition, co-exposure to other air pollutants, sex, APOE genotype, and epigenetic reprogramming. Overall, the present review proposes an integrated multi-organ model of PM2.5 neurotoxicity that aligns environmental exposure with key mechanisms of AD pathogenesis and highlights priorities for strengthening causal inference and future translational research.

C3.title: (1)H MRS reveals impact of early adversity and age on neurometabolic profiles in women
C3.abstract: Exposure to early-life stress (ELS), including neglect or abuse, is known for its detrimental effects on brain health. This study investigated how ELS interacts with chronological age to impact on brain metabolism in middle-aged women using proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H MRS) at 3 T. High-quality spectra from the hippocampus (HC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) from 75 women, including 53% with ELS exposure before puberty, were analyzed. Generalized additive models assessed non-linear effects of ELS severity and chronological age on neurometabolites related to neuroinflammation and neurotransmitter cycling. Significant interactions emerged for myo-inositol (Ins) in both regions and glutamine (Gln) in the PCC, where greater ELS severity was linked to age-related increases in Ins and Gln concentrations. These results were robust when additionally controlling for symptoms of depression, anxiety, and PTSD, as well as SES, education, menopause status, and smoking. The observed patterns suggest that ELS exposure before puberty, at the older age range, is associated with glial and glutamatergic alterations that are indicative of neuroinflammation, potentially reflecting vulnerability to adverse brain health outcomes.

C3.title: IL-17 aggravates the neuroinflammatory response in depression by regulating microglial polarization through the JAK1/STAT3 signaling pathway
C3.abstract: Background: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is closely related to the development of depression. As a proinflammatory cytokine, IL-17 plays a key role in various neuroinflammatory diseases. This study aimed to investigate the potential molecular mechanisms through which IL-17 affects neuroinflammation in depression through the regulation of microglial polarization. Methods: A chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced mouse model of depression and an LPS-treated BV2 cell model were used. The depression-like behavior of the mice was evaluated using the sucrose preference test (SPT), tail suspension test (TST), and forced swim test (FST). Neuronal injury was assessed using HE staining. The levels of neurotransmitters and inflammatory cytokines were analyzed using ELISA. Microglial polarization was analyzed by flow cytometry and immunofluorescence, and the expression of IL-17A and JAK1/STAT3 pathway-related proteins was assessed using Western blotting. C3.title: Beyond monoamines: a multi-systems molecular framework for major depressive disorder
C3.abstract: For over five decades, the monoamine hypothesis has anchored the conceptual and pharmacological approach to major depressive disorder (MDD), yet nearly one-third of patients fail to achieve remission with standard antidepressants, and therapeutic response is delayed by weeks. This narrative review offers a critical synthesis of recent high-impact literature drawn on evidence from genomic, molecular, and translational studies across six domains: genomic architecture, epigenetic dysregulation, neuroinflammation, neurotrophic signalling, gut-brain axis, and rapid-acting antidepressant mechanisms, to construct a multi-systems framework of MDD pathophysiology and, as a secondary and explicitly scoped aim, to identify translational priorities for South Asian, particularly Indian, populations; the evidence reviewed is global in scope. A 2025 genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 688,808 cases identified 697 independent associations mapping to 635 genomic risk loci implicating glutamatergic, GABAergic, and neuropeptidergic systems. An inflammatory MDD subgroup, characterised by kynurenine pathway disruption and microglial dysregulation, is of interest for patient stratification. Rapid-acting antidepressants proposed to act through TrkB-BDNF-dependent synaptic plasticity offer a mechanistic account of their fast onset, although the direct-binding theory awaits independent replication. C3.title: Differential role of Galectin-1 in neuronal stress and plasticity pathways
C3.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of impaired neuronal homeostasis involving complex interactions among oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and altered neuroplasticity. Galectin-1 (Gal-1), a multifunctional β-galactoside-binding lectin with neuroprotective and immunomodulatory properties, has emerged as a potential regulator of cellular homeostasis. However, its endogenous role in coordinating neuronal responses to cellular stress remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the contribution of endogenous Gal-1 to stress responses, inflammatory gene expression, and pathways associated with neuroplasticity and neurotransmission using an in vitro model of oxidative stress in human SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. Exposure to hydrogen peroxide (H2O2, 100 μM, 24 h) significantly reduced cell viability, increased reactive oxygen species production, and promoted apoptosis and necrosis, whereas fluoxetine co-treatment partially restored cell survival and reduced oxidative status. Notably, oxidative stress upregulated LGALS1 mRNA expression while concomitantly decreasing intracellular Gal-1 protein levels, indicating a divergence between transcriptional and protein responses. Functional neutralization of Gal-1 using a specific antibody significantly attenuated the stress- and fluoxetine-induced expression of key neuroplasticity genes (CREB1 and MAPK1) and neurotransmitter receptors (DRD1, DRD2, GRIN2B, and HTR2A), while displaying a divergent, condition-dependent upregulation of BDNF. Pharmacological inhibition of NMDA or dopamine D2 receptors did not alter Gal-1 protein levels, suggesting that Gal-1 operates independently or upstream of these classical receptors. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that Gal-1 acts as an integrative molecular node connecting cellular stress responses to neuroplasticity and neurotransmitter-related signaling programs, providing new mechanistic insights into neuronal resilience and stress-related neuropsychiatric disorders.

C3.title: Flavonoids as Prospective Therapeutic Agents in Targeting Neurotrophic Signalling, HPA Axis Dysregulation, and Neuroinflammation in Depression
C3.abstract: Depression is a complex neuropsychiatric condition marked by ongoing mood disruptions and is closely linked to the dysfunction of neurotrophic signalling, heightened activity of the Hypothalamic- Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress in the Central Nervous System (CNS). Even with traditional antidepressants accessible, factors like slow onset, side effects, and resistance to treatment require the investigation of alternative and supplementary therapeutic approaches. C3.title: Chinese herbal medicine formulas for Alzheimer's disease: Evidence, mechanisms, and translational standards
C3.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is defined biologically by amyloid and tau pathology. The emergence of biomarker-based diagnostic criteria, blood-based assays, and anti-amyloid therapeutic trials has substantially raised the evidentiary standard for all candidate AD interventions, including Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) formulas. However, CHM formula evidence for AD lacks critical appraisal and methodological standards. Thus, this review aims to: (1) critically evaluate the clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence for oral or topical CHM formulas used in AD, specifically those selected according to Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnostic; and (2) assess the methodological requirements necessary for credible development of such formulas in AD research. Most included studies relied on clinical diagnoses, likely encompassing mixed pathologies (e.g., vascular dementia, dementia with Lewy bodies, or depression-related cognitive impairment), rendering their results preliminary rather than confirmatory for biologically defined AD. Current evidence does not support CHM formulas as established therapies for AD. Future studies will require biomarker-confirmed diagnosis, rigorous formula quality control, prespecified TCM pattern stratification, clinically meaningful cognitive and functional endpoints, mechanistic target-engagement measures, and prospective safety and herb-drug interaction monitoring.

These findings highlight the importance of intervention timing for VitD3 efficacy and support precision nutrition strategies aligned with CR for stress disorders.

C4.title: Choroid plexus volume as a marker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness in major depressive disorder
C4.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is a core feature of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). Patients received total sleep deprivation plus light therapy (TSD + LT), consisting of three 36-hour sleep deprivation cycles, each separated by a night of recovery sleep. LT was administered for 30 min every morning. Depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and chronotype were assessed through Beck's Depression Inventory (BDI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), respectively. ChP volumes were extracted with FreeSurfer and normalized for intracranial volume. Effects of chronotherapeutics were assessed on BDI, PSQI, and ChP volumes, with treatment response as a between-subject factor. The efficacy of treatment was also investigated stratifying for chronotype. Also, group differences in ChP volume and associations with sleep and BDI scores were explored. TSD + LT reduced depressive symptoms and improved sleep quality, with changes in PSQI associated with symptom improvement. Eveningness predicted greater depressive symptom reduction. At baseline, responders already exhibited larger left ChP volume than controls. Following treatment, a treatment × response interaction emerged for right ChP volume, showing a significant reduction in responders. Finally, reductions in both right and left ChP volumes predicted clinical improvement, and sleep quality improvement predicted right ChP volume reduction. This is the first study showing that chronotherapy modulates ChP structure in MDD, suggesting a link between circadian dysregulation and ChP enlargement proportional to clinical improvement and predicted by sleep amelioration. ChP volume may represent a biomarker of treatment responsiveness and circadian realignment.

C4.title: Genetic Susceptibility, Neurodevelopmental Abnormalities, and Neuroimmune Interactions Across Major Psychiatric Disorders

We propose a multidimensional developmental-immune framework in which genetic liability, environmental exposure timing, and peripheral immune status jointly shape transdiagnostic trajectories. This framework reframes psychiatric disorders as dynamic interactions among stable trait-like susceptibilities and fluctuating biological states, offering a roadmap for biomarker-driven stratification and early immune-targeted interventions.

C4.title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder

Transcriptomic analyses further identified hippocampal matrix metalloproteinase-19 (MMP19) as a critical downstream effector, and genetic knockdown experiments confirmed its indispensability in the expression of manic-like behaviors. Collectively, these results delineate a previously unrecognized vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in BD pathophysiology, highlighting peripheral creatine metabolic routes as actionable targets for therapeutic intervention. Overall, this work provides compelling evidence that peripheral metabolic disturbances can drive central nervous system dysfunction via neuroimmune crosstalk, offering a new conceptual framework for understanding mood disorder etiology.

C4.title: Beyond the gut: neuroinflammation as a driver of anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
C4.abstract: Anxiety and depression frequently co-occur with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), with prevalence rates substantially higher than in the general population. Emerging evidence further indicates that active IBD is associated with more severe psychological symptoms, while anxiety and depression can worsen intestinal inflammation, highlighting a bidirectional relationship. Chronic intestinal inflammation is increasingly recognized as a driver of neuroinflammation, a key mechanism underlying mood disorders. In IBD, disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier permits metabolites and enteric signaling molecules to enter the circulation, triggering systemic inflammation and crossing the more permeable blood-brain barrier (BBB) to promote neuroinflammation. Other relevant components of the gut-brain axis contributing to IBD-associated neuroinflammation include the enteric nervous system, vagus nerve (VN), hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, and tryptophan-kynurenine metabolism. Within the brain, neuroinflammation characterized by glial activation, inflammatory mediator release, and oxidative stress disrupts neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity in regions such as the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, contributing to anxiety and depression. Conversely, anxiety and depression can amplify systemic inflammation through dysregulation of the VN and HPA axis, thereby exacerbating IBD. This reciprocal interaction adversely affects disease severity, quality of life, and therapeutic outcomes, underscoring the need to better define its underlying mechanisms. The present review synthesizes current clinical, translational, and experimental evidence on the bidirectional crosstalk between IBD and mood disorders. We also highlight key knowledge gaps, future research directions to identify the cellular and molecular mediators of this interaction, and emerging therapeutic strategies for the integrated management of both conditions.

C4.title: Sulforaphane alleviates DSS-induced colitis and gut-brain axis dysfunction potentially via microbiota-metabolism-HIF-1α crosstalk
C4.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract, often accompanied by anxiety- and depression-like symptoms, which are closely associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, metabolic disturbances, immune activation, and dysfunction of the gut-brain axis. Sulforaphane (SFN), a natural isothiocyanate, has been demonstrated in our previous studies to alleviate colitis in mice; however, its effects on UC-associated neurobehavioral abnormalities remain unclear. In this study, a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model was employed to investigate the effects of SFN on colitis and associated behavioral abnormalities. SFN significantly alleviated colitis symptoms and improved anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, accompanied by enhanced hippocampal structure and function. Mechanistically, SFN improved intestinal barrier integrity by increasing goblet cell abundance, upregulating MUC2 expression, and normalizing the expression of tight junction proteins, including Occludin, Claudin-1, Claudin-5, and ZO-1. SFN attenuated both peripheral and central inflammation responses and promoted anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization. In addition, SFN partially restored gut microbiota composition, increased short-chain fatty acid production, and improved amino acid and energy metabolism. DSS-induced colitis was associated with increased HIF-1α expression and glycolytic activation, whereas SFN inhibited HIF-1α signaling and downregulated the expression of glycolysis-related genes (Glut1, Pfkl, Ldha). GEO database analysis revealed that HIF-1α expression was significantly elevated in patients with active UC compared with both health controls and patients with inactive UC. Collectively, SFN ameliorates colitis and associated behavioral abnormalities, potentially through modulation of gut microbiota composition, metabolic reprogramming, and HIF-1α-related immunometabolic pathways.
